newsitem.title: USA: CardioThoracic CEO responds to report.
newsitem.headline: CardioThoracic CEO responds to report.

text.p: CardioThoracic Systems Inc Chief Executive Officer Rich Ferrari, responding a Barron's article, on Monday said the minimally invasive heart operation procedure developed by the company was in its infancy and its acceptance would grow as the technology improved.
CardioThoracic devised a system to operate on a beating heart. About 1,000 patients are expected undergo the procedure by the end of February, Ferrari said.
After the weekend report , CardioThoracic Systems shares fell 1-1/2 points to 21-3/4 by early afternoon on trading of 314,300 shares, compared with a daily average of 191,000.
Physicians told Barron's that CardioThoracic's procedure could be used in approximately five percent of bypass operations.
"We're in the infancy in a complete changeover of how a bypass procedure is performed," Ferrari said.
He noted that improvements in technology and other gains in the field should increase the number of physicians using the procedure.
"We'll let the results speak for themselves, because that's the thing that matters," Ferrari said.
